items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: I thought about Marshall for several days. I said, well, I better treat him right as an accompanist... I would call him up and ask him all the registers of his saxophone that he wanted to touch... And it turned out very well.

ctx.x: And about the part that Marshall Royal played, Marshall's solo in the radio scene.

Well, this was a thing where I'd learned some things from Ellington, to put the human element in the -- into the person -- into the horn and to take the notes off the paper, because the notes cannot play. You have to have the interpretation, you know? And Freddie Hubbard was sitting Here's a great big, what, 40 pieces, I guess. there. (Unintelligible) And he had what we call a cue, a part to play, and Shaft was making love to this lady, and Freddie was playing it as a typical jazz solo, which he's very adept at…

saxophone that he wanted to touch, didn't want to touch, or whatever. We just talked about it, you know, until I found out the key, or the style I wanted to do the accompaniment, you know. And it turned out very well.
